solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After a nap returned to order a cigar

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the two words are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to order someone is to tell them to do something

explanation.surface: Someone wakes from a nap and sends out for a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses A NAP; 'After' just joins the reversed nap to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long, slender type of cigar.

clue.text: A curmudgeon finally put in a few coins, showing remorse

indicators.note: put in tells us the letters before it are placed inside the coins

parts.note: pence are small British coins, so a few coins can be PENCE

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word curmudgeon

explanation.surface: A grumpy old person finally drops some coins in a collecting box, as if sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places A plus N, the last letter of curmudgeon, inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is the self-punishment that expresses sorrow for wrongdoing, so it stands for remorse.

clue.text: Local from NE coming round at four

indicators.note: coming round says the two letters sit around the rest, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of north-east
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A local person from the north-east turns up at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' makes the compass letters wrap the rest; four is a Roman numeral here.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a place is someone born there, a local inhabitant.

clue.text: Test in term: is able to appear regularly

indicators.note: letters that appear regularly are taken at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first

explanation.surface: An exam during the school term that shows whether a pupil is able.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of TERM IS ABLE, starting from T, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is an experiment or examination of something, a synonym for a test.

clue.text: Garland that is large put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting letters up means reading them from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big garland is hung up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns IE plus L into LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: All aboard on convertible, crossing motorway: it might move very slowly!

indicators.note: crossing says the shuffled letters are stretched across the motorway letter, holding it
something convertible can be changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A call to board an open-top car crossing the motorway, which then crawls along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' rearranges ALL ABOARD ON around M ('crossing'). An abnormal load is an oversized lorry cargo, usually escorted at low speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An abnormal load is an oversized cargo on a road vehicle, which typically travels at crawling speed.

clue.text: We must be engulfed in sadness: that's amazing!

indicators.note: engulfed in means swallowed up by, so the first word goes inside the second

parts.note: woe is grief or sadness

explanation.surface: A gloomy line about being overwhelmed by sorrow, then a cheerful exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be engulfed in' sends 'We' inside the sadness word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wowee is an informal exclamation of astonishment or delight.

clue.text: Surprised reaction from one in healthy state

parts.note: well means in good health
I is the Roman numeral for one
to state is to declare

explanation.surface: Someone in good health is startled by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in healthy' tempts a container, but the pieces simply run in order and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Well I declare' is an old-fashioned exclamation used to express astonishment.

clue.text: Turning up in Ratibati a wild, thorny plant

indicators.note: Turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer is concealed within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thorny shrub crops up somewhere wild with an exotic name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the concealed letters and 'Turning up', in a down clue, reads them from bottom to top. The draft lacked an indicator for the concealment; 'in' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wait-a-bit is a name for several hooked thorny shrubs, especially African acacias that snag passers-by.

clue.text: Crackers I turn to in food processing

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone reaches for crackers when it comes to eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like a snack food but is the anagram signal for I TURN TO IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is the process by which the body takes in and uses food.

clue.text: Girl I left in meadow

indicators.note: in says the preceding letters are placed within the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.surface: Someone recalls abandoning a girl in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I plus L inside LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Leila is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: One converting to book form, turning over lines

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer adapting something into a book flips through its lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges OVER LINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A noveliser adapts a film or play into the form of a novel.

clue.text: Nan's wild embraces much disturbed German composer

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the first group of letters surrounds the second
wild means out of control, so the letters of Nan's are mixed up
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled too

explanation.surface: An excited grandmother gives a troubled person a big hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns NANS into S...ANN, which 'embraces' CHUM, made by 'disturbed' from MUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a nineteenth-century German Romantic composer.

clue.text: Back in street, bedraggled person owed money

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer is concealed within the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scruffy creditor is back on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the concealed letters and 'Back' reads them in reverse. The draft lacked an indicator for the concealment; 'in' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: A debtee is the creditor, the party to whom a debt is due.

clue.text: A lieutenant: he meets a lady

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An army officer is introduced to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Althea is a woman's first name, so it fits a lady.

clue.text: Buddhist monk taking in sinful erotic dance

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the monk's letters go round the next word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
bad means wicked or sinful

explanation.surface: A monk lets in some sinful, sensual dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' means the monk's letters hold the sinful word.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian dance famous for close, sensual partner contact.

clue.text: Italian resort: in one south of border

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so these letters follow the border word

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seaside town in Italy lies just below a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' puts IN plus I below RIM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside holiday town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Religious instruction for Catholic? Problem is Mass without English

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other letters sit around the English letter

parts.note: a catch is a hidden problem or snag

explanation.surface: A worry that Catholic teaching leaves the Mass without English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like removal but has its old sense of outside: the other pieces wrap round E, and no letter is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a question-and-answer summary of doctrine used to teach Christians, notably Catholics.

clue.text: In need of repair, once, a boat

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A boat that once was in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In need of repair' rearranges ONCE A.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light, narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Don't vote for this party?

parts.note: read as advice to vote against; it is also slang for a lively party

explanation.surface: An election slogan urging people not to back a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as BE A NO, voting against, while 'party' is not political but a knees-up. A beano is British slang for a party or spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Country fellow at home, visiting a Royal Academician

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so these letters are put inside the others

parts.note: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a gent is a man or fellow
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man staying in calls on a distinguished artist in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' sends the fellow and 'at home' inside A plus the Academician's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America.

clue.text: Stuff that's sweet and endlessly virtuous?

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: good means virtuous

explanation.surface: A sickly sweet substance that seems almost too good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the D from GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a sticky substance, and also cloying sentimentality, so it can be sugary stuff.

clue.text: Row with newspaper boss ended fast?

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or row
ed is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An argument with the editor ended quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but means going without food; eating a meal ends a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a meal, which brings any period of not eating to an end.

clue.text: Trio cease perversely making things obscure

indicators.note: perversely means in a contrary, twisted way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three performers stubbornly refuse to stop, making things murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversely' rearranges TRIO CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are items of specialised knowledge understood only by a few, hence obscure matters.
